page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1ne.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor. The virtual machine is powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor, presenting 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Its CPU cache structure consists of 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache. It incorporates instruction set extensions including AVX, AVX-512F, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA.

System memory is configured at 8.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance carries no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached block storage volumes for persistent data operations. Networking provides a baseline throughput of 2 Gbps, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default. No hardware graphics accelerators are present, limiting acceleration tasks strictly to host CPU instruction execution.

Benchmark results reflect legacy generation characteristics. PassMark CPU tests yield a score of 3619.18, alongside a single-core Geekbench score of 896.0 and multi-core score of 1975.0, positioning core throughput in the bottom tier of cloud compute. Memory throughput registers 19.1 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 17.26 GB/sec for writes. Redis throughput achieves 2.87 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput measures 2.43 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the hardware profile offers entry-level compute resources at an accessible entry tier, though its older CPU microarchitecture yields lower performance density per vCPU compared to newer generation platforms. The instance is suitable for low-intensity batch jobs, basic web serving, development or staging environments, and legacy backend tasks that require dedicated vCPU allocation without high compute or memory bandwidth demands.

Hyper-threaded across 2 physical cores, the configuration supplies 2.0 GB of memory per core and includes hardware support for AVX and AVX-512F instructions. The server contains no local storage and does not include GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached storage and standard network links rated at a 2 Gbps baseline. Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate lower-tier computing throughput, indicated by a Geekbench multi-core score of 1975.0 and PassMark CPU score of 3619.18. Due to its balanced compute ratio and dedicated vCPU scheduling, this instance serves non-critical infrastructure, basic web servers, lightweight background worker services, and staging environments.
